chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Aban ibn Taghlib who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave girl, then married her to another man, so she bore children from him. Then her husband died and left children from her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her children are like her status. So when the one who emancipated their mother dies, they are free.'
I said to him: 'Is it permissible for the one who emancipated their mother to retract his emancipation if he is in need?' He said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'What is your view if their mother dies after the husband, and her children from the free husband remain? Is it permissible for her master to sell her children and retract the emancipation regarding them?' He said: 'No. Rather, he may only retract the emancipation of their mother if he is in need and she is pleased with that.'

key_terms.أُمَّهُمْ: Their mother (referring to the slave girl)
key_terms.دَبَّرَ: Emancipated (specifically referring to the declaration of freedom for a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the emancipation of a slave girl's children if the master retracts her freedom?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'tadbir' (conditional emancipation), clarifying that while the master may retract the mother's freedom if she consents, the children's status remains permanently free as they are 'ahrar' (freeborn). It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the revocable status of the mother and the irrevocable freedom of her offspring, ensuring their lineage is not diminished by the master's subsequent needs.
